issue.name: SQL injection
issue.issueBackground: SQL injection vulnerabilities arise when user-controllable data is incorporated into database SQL queries in an unsafe manner.
issue.remediationBackground: The most effective way to prevent SQL injection attacks is to use parameterized queries (also known as prepared statements) for all database access.
issue.issueDetail: The id parameter appears to be vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. A single quote was submitted in the id parameter, and a database error message was returned.

issue.name: Cross-site scripting (reflected)
issue.issueBackground: Reflected cross-site scripting vulnerabilities arise when data is copied from a request and echoed into the application's immediate response in an unsafe way.
issue.remediationBackground: In most situations where user-controllable data is copied into application responses, cross-site scripting attacks can be prevented using two layers of defenses: input validation and output encoding.
issue.issueDetail: The value of the name request parameter is copied into the HTML document as plain text between tags. The payload was echoed unmodified in the application's response.

issue.name: OS command injection
issue.issueBackground: Operating system command injection vulnerabilities arise when an application incorporates user-controllable data into a command that is processed by a shell command interpreter.
issue.remediationBackground: If possible, applications should avoid incorporating user-controllable data into operating system commands.
issue.issueDetail: The ip parameter appears to be vulnerable to OS command injection attacks. The application executed the injected command and returned its output.

issue.name: Cookie without HttpOnly flag set
issue.issueBackground: If the HttpOnly attribute is set on a cookie, then the cookie's value cannot be read or set by client-side JavaScript.
issue.remediationBackground: There is usually no good reason not to set the HttpOnly flag on all cookies.
issue.issueDetail: The following cookie was issued by the application and does not have the HttpOnly flag set: PHPSESSID

issue.name: Frameable response (potential clickjacking)
issue.issueBackground: If a page fails to set an appropriate X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy HTTP header, it might be possible for a page controlled by an attacker to load it within an iframe.
issue.remediationBackground: To effectively prevent framing attacks, the application should return a response header with the name X-Frame-Options and the value DENY.
issue.issueDetail: The response does not include either an X-Frame-Options header or a Content-Security-Policy header with a frame-ancestors directive.
